selection: Six previously unused Zod fixes selected from PR title/body and merge SHA only. No fixing diff was opened before this file was frozen.

cases.issue: A discriminated union fails to route an absent discriminator to the sole option whose discriminator schema permits omission. An omittable discriminator must claim undefined, while an ordinary present discriminator must keep routing normally.

A derived exact-optional constructor loses its lazy override, so template-literal matching treats the exact-optional literal as if undefined were a valid value. The derived lazy value must override the base while a present literal remains accepted.

Input-mode JSON Schema shortens tuple minItems when a required slot is wrapped in preprocess. Requiredness must resolve through the wrapper, while a genuinely optional trailing slot must still shorten minItems.
cases.target: import * as z from "../packages/zod/src/v4/index.ts";const schema=z.tuple([z.string(),z.preprocess((v)=>v,z.string())]);const json=z.toJSONSchema(schema,{io:"input"}) as any;console.log(json.minItems===2);
cases.control: import * as z from "../packages/zod/src/v4/index.ts";const schema=z.tuple([z.string(),z.string().optional()]);const json=z.toJSONSchema(schema,{io:"input"}) as any;console.log(json.minItems===1);

cases.issue: Input-mode JSON Schema keeps an output-typed catch fallback above a transforming schema. The emitter must strip that default, while a non-transforming string catch keeps its valid string default.
cases.target: import * as z from "../packages/zod/src/v4/index.ts";const schema=z.string().transform((v)=>v.length).pipe(z.number()).catch(0);const json=z.toJSONSchema(schema,{io:"input"}) as any;console.log(!("default" in json)&&json.type==="string");

cases.issue: The object JIT fast path retains a value written beside a swallowed issue for an absent optional key. A successful parse must omit that value, while the interpreted path remains unchanged.

An intersection rejects an object-owned key because the record operand's regex key schema is applied to every key. The intersection must accept keys governed by either operand, while the standalone record must still reject a nonmatching key.
